claims.head: Stars collide: Aho vs. Knies
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ L1 (Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov) spends at least 44% of its 5-on-5 time against the Blue Jackets’ first line, against about 29% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Aho’s line (Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Blue Jackets’ first line is Knies, Coyle and Olivier.
claims.nums: At home: 58% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 29% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Blue Jackets’ first line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Carolina home games this season · 5 games, 35 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 29% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: The Hurricanes should drive the play
claims.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blue Jackets around the middle. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Blue Jackets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes should be in control
CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Blue Jackets’ best way in is getting good looks.

CBJ.head: The Blue Jackets are up against it
CBJ.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Blue Jackets’ best hope is getting good looks, plus a big night from Jet Greaves.

paras: Both teams have won two in a row.

items.text: Pyotr Kochetkov has won all eight of his starts this season, matching Frederik Andersen (2021-22) for the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history. One more win would make it his alone.
Jesperi Kotkaniemi has a point in seven straight games against Columbus, with a goal in each of the last three.
The Blue Jackets are newly without Emil Andrae, and have had to make do without Ivan Provorov all season.
The Hurricanes have been without Taylor Hall since Oct 13.
